problem: Source: "I could not soon recover myself" - she could not recover quickly. MODERN "I could not recover myself" drops "soon" and makes it absolute.
new_text: I rose up suddenly, terrified by the solitude that so ruthless a judge haunted—by the silence that so awful a voice filled. My head swam as I stood upright. I realized I was growing faint from agitation and hunger; I had eaten and drunk nothing all day, having skipped breakfast. And with a strange pang, I now reflected that, long as I had been shut in here, no one had sent a message to ask how I was or to invite me downstairs. Not even little Adèle had knocked at the door. Not even Mrs. Fairfax had come looking for me. "Friends always forget those whom fortune abandons," I murmured, as I unbolted the door and stepped out. I stumbled over an obstacle—my head was still dizzy, my vision dim, and my limbs feeble. I could not quickly recover myself. I fell, but not to the ground: an outstretched arm caught me. I looked up—I was being held by Mr. Rochester, who sat in a chair across my bedroom threshold.

problem: Source: "then I should not have to make the effort of cracking my heart-strings in rending them from among Mr. Rochester's" - the image is of her heart-strings entwined among his, and the 'effort' she dreads. MODERN "crack my heartstrings in tearing them away from Mr. Rochester" drops both the effort and the entwining ('from among Mr. Rochester's').
new_text: "I cannot. I am tired and sick. I want some water." He let out a sort of shuddering sigh, and taking me in his arms, carried me downstairs. At first I did not know what room he had brought me to; everything was blurred to my glazed sight. Soon I felt the reviving warmth of a fire; for, summer as it was, I had grown ice-cold in my room. He put wine to my lips; I tasted it and revived. Then I ate something he offered me, and was soon myself again. I was in the library—sitting in his chair—he was very close. "If I could leave this life now, without too sharp a pang, it would be well for me," I thought. "Then I would not have to make the effort of cracking my heartstrings in tearing them loose from among Mr. Rochester's. I must leave him, it seems. I do not want to leave him—I cannot leave him."

problem: Source: "you wanted to read the tablet of one's heart" - biblical phrase (Proverbs 3:3, 2 Cor. 3:3). MODERN "read the very heart itself" loses the scriptural image; the project voice rule asks to keep biblical language.
new_text: "When you are curious, Jane, you always make me smile. You open your eyes like an eager bird and shift restlessly now and then, as if words in speech don't come fast enough for you and you want to read the tablet of one's heart. But before I go on, tell me what you mean by your 'Well, sir?' It is a little phrase you use constantly, and many a time it has drawn me on and on through endless talk. I am not sure why."
